content.text:
I couldn't reproduce the auto-grow problem in tests. I fixed the most likely cause and added a safety net, but I haven't confirmed the fix in the running app. If it still misbehaves, tell me what you see: an empty row, the last row cut off, or a jump while typing.

**What I tested:** I checked the input's height against where the editor actually draws the text:
- short text, trailing newlines, wrapped prose, indented lines, list items, one very long unbroken word, tabs, emoji and wide characters;
- typing past the 12-row limit and deleting back down.

In every case the height matched exactly, with no row cut off and no empty row.

**Likely cause:** the input works out its height before drawing by wrapping the text itself, using a plain version of the monospace font. The editor wraps using the full font it inherits from its surroundings, which can differ in weight, font features or fallback fonts. Where those differ, the two disagree on where a line wraps. Depending on the text, that leaves one row too few (the last line cut off or scrolled) or one too many (an empty row). The test font happens to match, which is why nothing showed up in tests.

**Fix, in `src/growing_input.rs`:** this is shared by the chat input, the commit message box, the spec form's description and the settings prompts.
- It now counts rows using the exact font the editor last drew in.
- After each redraw it checks how many rows the editor actually used. If that differs from its estimate, it takes the editor's count, so any leftover mismatch corrects itself by the next frame instead of staying wrong.

**Spec:** the growing text input spec now says rows are counted as the input itself lays out its text, in its own font, so no row is ever cut off or left empty.

**Tests:**
- A new test forces the estimate to be two rows too high, then two too low, and checks the input settles on the real layout. It fails with the correction turned off.
- 274 of 275 pass; the one failure is the same `...`/`…` default-prompt test as before.
